newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA TO RESUME NATIONAL SOCCER CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA TO RESUME NATIONAL SOCCER CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Bulgaria's soccer championship resumes this weekend, overshadowed by a miserable performance by the country's two top teams in European soccer.

Champions CSKA Sofia, who have produced players such as Hristo Stoichkov and Emil Kostadinov, lost hope of qualifying for the European Cup when they went down 2-0 to Romania's Steaua Bucharest in Sofia on Wednesday.
Neftochimik Bourgas, which came second in the championship last season, lost its UEFA Cup first preliminary round tie on aggregate despite beating Norway's Brann Bergen 3-2 in Bourgas the same night.
Football fans are now hoping Levski Sofia will do better at home to Slovakia's Slovan Bratislava in a qualifying round tie of the European Cup Winners' Cup on August 14.

With the top clubs failing to make it to Europe's soccer stadiums, the only hope lies with the national team. The 1994 World Cup semifinalists have a chance of qualifying for the 1998 World Cup finals ahead of their Group Five ties against Israel on August 20 and Russia on September 10 and October 11.
"It is clear...that European work can not be done with a provincial mentality," sports newspaper Seven Days Sport said on Thursday, refering to CSKA's performance.
Neftochimik Bourgas lost its sponsor this week when the new management of the debt-ridden Neftochim oil refinery said it could no longer sponsor the club due to a lack of funds.
The plant spent some 1.5 billion levs on Neftochimik in 1996 and the first five months of this year, and built a modern football stadium in Bourgas at a cost of 1.9 billion levs.
Club president Hristo Portochanov said the club would now be forced to seek a quick transfer for its top player and captain Radostin Kishishev in a bid to win some funds.
"There are some alternatives such as to change the name of the team and seek a strong sponsor," Portochanov told Standard daily newspaper in an interview.
The Bourgas players are threatening to boycott their first match in the championship on Sunday in a protest against the refinery chiefs' plans to replace Portochanov.
However, soccer analysts expect surprises from the three newcomers in the first division Litex Lovech, Metalurg Pernik and Olympic Galata.

Levski Sofia new coach Stefan Grozdanov said Litex would be among the six teams battling for the champion's title. Apart from his team, the remaining bidders are CSKA Sofia, Slavia Sofia, Lokomotiv Sofia and Neftochimik Bourgas, he added.
Sofia's Lokomotiv is also expected to show a new face in the new season after head coach Hristo Bonev started training the team last month.
